basis: Read install-skill.ts (src/core/skills/install-skill.ts), FR-FLOW-024/025/026/027/028/029/030 in docs/spec/60.workflow-release.srs.md, and the 2-axis eval report + axis_a_r8/axis_b_r8. Judged each decision by 'how smooth and error-resistant is it when an agent/user actually runs the skill/tool', maintenance cost, and reuse of existing machinery.

decisions.topic: install-skill does not materialize _shared/kiwi mirror at destination
decisions.alt_proposal: Complete the design already half-built in install-skill.ts: during executeOne, also copy the files returned by collectSharedResourceReferences (deduplicated across all skills in one install run) into destinationRoot/_shared/kiwi/, transactionally (same stage+backup+rename pattern), and record their checksums. Do NOT add a new subcommand or a separate 'install shared' path — the reference-collection (collectSharedResourceReferences) and the target location (sharedResourceRoot) already exist; only the copy step is missing. Optionally add a post-install parity assertion that every collected reference resolves at destination, failing SKILL_INSTALL rather than shipping a dangling skill.
decisions.rationale: This is not a preference gap, it is a broken-on-arrival bug. (1) SKILL_NAME_PATTERN (/^[A-Za-z0-9].../) rejects '_shared' and selector=all skips '_'-prefixed dirs, so the tool CANNOT install shared resources by any path — manual cp is the only option, which defeats the install tool's entire purpose. (2) Metadata already writes sharedResourceRoot=destination/_shared/kiwi and sharedResourceValidation, i.e. the tool implies the mirror exists while never creating it. Every kiwi-* skill referencing ../_shared/kiwi/{mini-option,auto-option,local-llm-profile}.md is dangling after a fresh-dest install. Efficiency-when-used: the first real use of the tool on a clean project silently produces a non-working skill. Manual workaround (c) is the exact footgun the tool should remove; requirement-only (b) leaves the tool broken until later.
decisions.execution_note: New follow-up SRS requirement (v2.3.0.x tool-improvement), NOT part of the current 11-req finalization — keep it out of the release commit. Fix reuses existing functions; ~small surface. TDD: add install-skill test asserting destinationRoot/_shared/kiwi/<referenced file> exists and checksum-matches after installing a skill that references it, to a fresh dest.
decisions.fidelity_impact: Directly serves the project purpose ('SRS is good but the code is implemented wrong -> fix it'): this is code that contradicts what its own metadata promises. High fidelity gain, restores tool correctness.

decisions.topic: -qna (active force) vs --qna (deprecated) single/double-dash footgun in FR-FLOW-024/028
decisions.alt_proposal: Rename the force flag from single-dash '-qna' to explicit double-dash '--qna-force'. Un-deprecate nothing: keep bare '--qna' as a deprecated alias but make it emit a one-line deprecation notice (NOT a silent no-op) that points to '--qna-force'. Update FR-FLOW-024 AC-2 and FR-FLOW-028 AC-2 token, the kiwi-srs/kiwi-pipeline arg parsing, and the 2 content tests.
decisions.rationale: The current split is the worst ergonomic shape: the ACTIVE force flag is the non-standard single-dash '-qna' while the standard-looking '--qna' is the DEPRECATED one — inverted from every convention (getopt reads -qna as -q -n -a). The failure mode is silent: a user types the natural '--qna' expecting to force the unbounded loop, gets a deprecated no-op, and the run proceeds WITHOUT forced qna with no error. Silent-wrong-behavior is high-severity even though the flag's usage frequency is low (most runs use --auto or default-on qna). '--qna-force' is self-documenting and cannot be confused with the deprecated alias. Crucially this is cheapest NOW: v2.3.0.1 is not yet committed/released, so no muscle memory exists yet — deferring makes the rename a breaking change for early adopters instead of a free pre-release cleanup.
decisions.execution_note: Small, localized amendment (flag token in 2 ACs + 2 skill files + ~2 tests). It lightly reopens the converged 2-axis loop, so a targeted re-run of the FR-FLOW-024/028 content tests suffices — no full loop. If the committee prefers zero release-reopen, fallback is (b) keep + document, but I rate the silent-failure risk high enough to justify the pre-release fix.
decisions.fidelity_impact: Ergonomics/correctness gain; removes a silent divergence between intent (force qna) and effect (no-op). Neutral-to-positive on SRS fidelity (AC wording becomes clearer).

decisions.topic: FR-FLOW-029 kiwi-wave-master worktree isolation (--wt removed for lack of rationale)
decisions.alt_proposal: Reintroduce '--wt' on kiwi-wave-master but with a SINGLE worktree for the ENTIRE wave sequence (not per-wave). kiwi-wave-master creates one dedicated worktree, runs every wave's /kiwi-pipeline INSIDE it while SUPPRESSING each per-wave pipeline's own --wt, and resolves merge-or-PR ONCE at the end (interactive ask / --auto -> kiwi-commit-auto-pr), mirroring FR-FLOW-027's resolution semantics at the sequence level. Add this as a new AC on FR-FLOW-029.
decisions.rationale: I explicitly REJECT the team-lead's hinted alt (let FR-FLOW-027's --wt just propagate per-wave). Decisive fact: FR-FLOW-029 waves are sequential and DEPENDENT — wave N+1 builds on wave N's code. Per-wave independent worktrees off base would make wave 2 unable to see wave 1's un-merged changes, breaking dependent waves (or forcing a merge between every wave, which fragments one epic into N PRs and N review cycles). A single sequence-level worktree preserves both wave dependency correctness AND base-branch safety, and per-wave scoped SRS targets are orthogonal to git isolation so they still work. Efficiency-when-used: one isolated branch + one clean merge/PR for the whole epic is what a user running a big autonomous wave effort actually wants; N worktrees/N PRs is friction, and per-wave-off-base is silently wrong.
decisions.execution_note: New follow-up SRS requirement (v2.3.0.x); do NOT block the current release — FR-FLOW-029 with --wt removed has no broken behavior, just a missing feature. When implemented, the per-wave pipeline must detect it is running under a wave-owned worktree and skip creating its own. TDD around 'single worktree created once, waves see prior wave's changes, one resolution at end'.
decisions.fidelity_impact: Adds capability that matches FR-FLOW-029's stated sequential/dependent semantics; the propagation alt would have contradicted them. Positive fidelity — the design follows the requirement's own dependency model.

decisions.topic: kiwi-hot-fix -> kiwi-srs-sync propagation asymmetry (claude synthesizes --auto-apply --yes-all; codex/etc prohibited)
decisions.alt_proposal: Register a follow-up SRS requirement for a SINGLE unified auto-apply policy across all agent variants, with the direction gated on a fact-check: IF codex/etc kiwi-srs-sync have dry-run-first + SRS mutation lock + validation parity with claude, unify PERMISSIVE (option b: all variants auto-apply under --auto, consistent with FR-FLOW-025's '--auto auto-decides rather than blocks' philosophy). IF they lack that safety parity, unify RESTRICTIVE (option a: claude also gates, so no variant auto-applies SRS mutation unattended). As an immediate cheap stopgap, apply (c): document the current asymmetry as a known per-agent limitation so doc-authors don't over-promise 'hot-fix --auto syncs SRS' uniformly.
decisions.rationale: The real defect is not which direction — it is that behavior DIVERGES BY AGENT for the same command, which is inherently un-reasoned-about: a doc author or agent cannot state one truth about 'hot-fix --auto'. Efficiency-when-used: on claude, hot-fix --auto completes SRS sync end-to-end; on codex/etc the same invocation fixes code then the srs-sync HALTS for a gate, silently breaking the --auto autonomy promise and leaving a stalled sync the user must return to. The fix is a UNIFIED policy, not a per-agent patch. I do not fabricate the safety facts — the direction must be decided by verifying codex/etc srs-sync gate parity, which is exactly why this is business/safety-decision territory and belongs in a deliberate SRS requirement, not an ad-hoc flip.
decisions.execution_note: Out of v2.3.0.1 scope (pre-existing asymmetry, not introduced by the 11 reqs) — do not block release. Sequence: (c) document now (one paragraph, near-zero cost), then (d) a new requirement whose AC encodes the unified policy + the safety-parity precondition. Someone must read the three srs-sync variants' gate code before choosing b vs a.
decisions.fidelity_impact: Converts an accidental per-agent divergence into a single stated policy — improves cross-variant fidelity and predictability. Neutral on current-release fidelity since it is out of scope.

decisions.topic: Follow-up sequencing: commit / verified transition / push / exit
decisions.alt_proposal: Order: (1) COMMIT the 11 implemented reqs + eval artifacts now as a durable checkpoint (working tree is dirty and at risk; commit message per global rules — no signatures, no phase/step markers in the title). (2) VERIFIED transition per-requirement with cited evidence — NOT a bulk flip: each of the 11 reqs cites its axis_a_r8 per_req 'full' entry + axis_b_r8 substantive_clean + regression 148/148, via the tool (add_verification_evidence + update_status, or kiwi-review-fix-loop --close-reqs which enforces the same). This is defensible precisely because per-req evidence exists; a bulk-finalize without it is forbidden. Commit the SRS status change. (3) PUSH once, covering both commits. (4) EXIT and notify completion via doculight (per standing preference). Record D1-D4 as separate v2.3.0.x SRS follow-up candidates — do NOT bundle them into the release commit or block push on them.
decisions.rationale: Efficiency + process-correctness: commit-before-push protects converged work immediately; the eval already CONVERGED, so bias to action — do not gold-plate or re-open for the deferred D1-D4. Verified must be evidence-backed per-req (the SRS workflow explicitly forbids bulk-finalize without per-req evidence + stability gate), but here the 2-axis loop produced exactly that per-req evidence, so the transition is legitimate if each req cites it rather than being swept. One push at the end minimizes remote churn. Keeping D1-D4 as separate follow-ups keeps each changed line traceable to one request and avoids a fat mixed commit.
decisions.execution_note: All 11 reqs are Stability=evolving (gate-passable). Verify countsByStatus/stabilityBlockers via summarize_target before the verified transition. If any single req lacks clean per-req evidence, leave it 'implemented' rather than force it — partial verified is fine.
decisions.fidelity_impact: Preserves the no-bulk-finalize governance while still recognizing genuine convergence evidence. High process fidelity.

overall: Efficiency-when-used reframes three of five: D1 is a real broken-on-arrival tool bug (the mirror is uninstallable by any path, and metadata already implies it exists) -> fix, high priority follow-up. D2's footgun is silent-wrong-behavior and is cheapest to fix pre-release -> rename to --qna-force. D3's better design is a SINGLE sequence-level worktree, and I reject per-wave propagation because dependent waves would break. D4's true defect is per-agent divergence, not direction -> unify via one policy (document now, requirement to unify, direction per safety-parity fact-check). D5: commit now, verified per-req evidence (never bulk), one push, exit; keep D1-D4 as separate follow-ups that must not block the release. Net: only D2 warrants a small pre-release amendment; D1/D3/D4 are correctness-improving follow-ups; the release itself should ship now.
